profile.reading: This two-building Houston, Texas campus (HOU3 at 11003 Corporate Centre Dr, HOU4 at 5160 Westway Park Blvd, both 77041) was built and originally operated by CyrusOne, which had published combined specifications of 347,000 sq ft and 84 MW of IT capacity (HOU3: 174,000 sq ft with a 3-Globe Green Globes certification; HOU4: 173,000 sq ft with a 2-Globe Green Globes certification). Multiple independent sources confirm CyrusOne sold this campus: CyrusOne's own press release announced a definitive agreement in January 2022 to divest its Houston assets, Data Center Frontier and Connect CRE both reported DataBank as the buyer of four Houston data centers for $670 million, and a further CyrusOne press release confirmed the sale closed in March 2022; DataBank's own website independently confirms it now operates these Houston facilities under the CyrusOne Houston name in its own portfolio history. This registry had carried this row under an unresolved CyrusOne-vs-unknown-buyer flag through 2026-09-02; this session resolved that flag with DataBank confirmed as the current operator via press coverage and DataBank's own site, and the row is corrected accordingly rather than left misattributed to CyrusOne, which no longer operates this campus. DataBank was founded in 2007 and, per its own materials, has grown into a private colocation, cloud, and interconnection provider with dozens of data centers across the US; the Houston acquisition added CyrusOne's former HOU3/HOU4 buildings to DataBank's existing Texas footprint alongside its Dallas and Plano facilities tracked elsewhere in this registry. The building-level sqft/MW figures above reflect CyrusOne's last published specifications prior to the 2022 sale and have not been independently reconfirmed as DataBank's current operating figures for the campus.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Houston publishes 84 MW of IT capacity across two buildings totaling 347,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 84 MW of IT load is roughly 2,100 racks. This campus ranks first among the 18 Texas facilities with published capacity figures and accounts for 18% of the 468 MW of total published data center IT capacity in the state.

HOU3 holds a 3-Globe Green Globes certification and HOU4 holds a 2-Globe certification, qualifying both for energy-efficient operations. The certifications do not specify whether the campus can host GPU-intensive workloads or the power density it is designed to deliver to individual racks. Without rack-level power specifications, the site's actual utility for large-scale AI compute deployment remains unclear.

CyrusOne divested its Houston assets in March 2022 for 670 million dollars, but the acquiring party name was not confirmed in available sources this session. CyrusOne's own operator page as of September 2026 still brands and lists full specifications for HOU3-HOU4 under the CyrusOne name, consistent with continued CyrusOne branding or operation, though this does not resolve the ownership status after the 2022 transaction. Ownership verification remains flagged for a future research pass.
